items.body: In classical Gnosticism, gnosis meant direct knowing of the divine spark — not scavenged lore or online mystique. Treat ‘forbidden knowledge’ as a call to inner clarity: what you actually know about your day, your will, and your next clear move — not what you scroll.

items.hed: As Above, So Below — Morning Edition
items.body: The Hermetic axiom from the Emerald Tablet isn’t astrology cosplay; it’s correspondence. Outer order (breath steady, body woken, desk clear) mirrors inner order. Align the micro ritual with the macro intention and the ‘magic’ is simply coherence.

items.hed: The Magician’s First Tool Is Timing
items.body: Western ceremonial magick obsesses over hours and elections because will without timing dissipates. Same rule for a Monday: cast the charge before the noise, not during it. Timing is the circle; attention is the charge.

items.hed: Siri AI rolls out in English with iOS 27 today; five more languages in October
items.body: Apple confirmed Siri AI launches with iOS 27 / iPadOS 27 on Monday, Sep 14, initially in English only, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish due in October. The assistant stays in beta with daily server-side usage caps, EU/China limits, and a future paid tier for expanded access that Apple has not yet priced.

items.hed: Altman joins Amodei and Musk in call to ‘pace the frontier’ — ‘we could lose control’
items.body: On Monday OpenAI’s Sam Altman welcomed a federal safety framework for frontier labs after weekend alignment with Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and Elon Musk on slowing capability races. Altman said pacing is not stopping, warned of losing control of the future to AI or concentrating power in one company, and backed independent evaluators with employee-like access; Trump dismissed a slowdown as risking the U.S. lead over China.

items.hed: Musk delays Grok 4.7, blaming an RL length penalty that makes the model quit early
items.body: Elon Musk said on Sep 11 that Grok 4.7 needs ‘a few more days to cook’ because xAI’s reinforcement-learning reward over-penalized response length, teaching the model to abandon hard but solvable tasks and skimp on self-checking. Grok 4.6 (shipped Aug 12) remains the current released flagship; no new ship date, model card, or API ID for 4.7 has been published.

items.hed: Anthropic says it blocked Claude misuse that could have aided bioweapons research
items.body: Anthropic’s Sep 10 threat-intel report details disrupted misuse of Claude from Dec 2025–Aug 2026 across cyber ops, surveillance, scams, influence campaigns, and dual-use biological research — including a blocked grant-application request involving gain-of-function work on chikungunya. The company says it hardened safeguards on newer models and shared findings with authorities and industry partners.

items.hed: Ballmer apologizes, says Clippers will comply with NBA’s historic cap sanctions
items.body: On Sunday Steve Ballmer reversed course and said L.A. will accept the league’s penalties — including a $30M fine, five forfeited first-round picks (2029–33), his one-year suspension, and executive bans — after Wachtell Lipton found $66M in cash/equity arrangements tied to Kawhi Leonard. Ballmer apologized to fans, staff, and owners and said the fine is paid and the chapter must close.

items.hed: Kawhi-to-Raptors trade still not filed as Clippers hunt interim governor
items.body: Even after Ballmer’s compliance statement, the Clippers have not named an interim governor to authorize completing the Kawhi Leonard deal to Toronto. Both sides expect the trade; Leonard has worked Raptors minicamps but remains limited until paperwork clears.

items.hed: Udoka: Fred VanVleet ramping hard toward Rockets return after ACL year
items.body: Houston coach Ime Udoka said VanVleet has stepped up rehab in San Diego with back-to-backs and contact work after missing all of 2025–26 with a torn right ACL. The veteran exercised his ~$25M player option to stay; Rockets won 52 without him last year but exited in the first round.

items.hed: Bears set franchise opener record in 59–37 demolition of Panthers
items.body: Caleb Williams threw for 269 and ran for 65 with four total TDs as Chicago piled up 552 yards and eight touchdowns in Charlotte. D’Andre Swift (124 rush, 3 TDs) and Kyle Monangai (100, 1 TD) powered a ground game that broke open a back-and-forth contest.

items.hed: Dart, Likely, Nabers lift Giants past Cowboys 28–20 in Harbaugh’s debut
items.body: Jaxson Dart went 23-of-29 for 230 yards and three TDs as New York converted 9-of-10 third downs and held the ball nearly 37 minutes in John Harbaugh’s first game. Isaiah Likely had 8/78/2; Malik Nabers returned from ACL surgery with 6/69.

items.hed: MNF Week 1: Broncos at Chiefs — Mahomes and Nix both returning from major injuries
items.body: Denver visits Kansas City tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC. Patrick Mahomes is back after a Week 15 ACL tear; Bo Nix returns from a Divisional Round broken ankle. Storylines include KWIII as KC’s workhorse and remade secondaries on both sides.

items.hed: Garcia crushes Benn in two rounds, retains WBC welterweight title
items.body: In Las Vegas on Sep 13, Ryan Garcia dropped Conor Benn with a right hand in round two and forced a stoppage at 1:25 of the round in his first WBC welterweight defense. Garcia then traded words with Teófimo López ringside.

items.hed: Noche UFC: Silva submits Delgado; Grasso outpoints Fiorot in Glendale
items.body: On Sep 12 at Desert Diamond Arena, Jean Silva finished Jose Miguel Delgado via rear-naked choke at 2:57 of Round 3. Alexa Grasso took a unanimous decision over Manon Fiorot (29–28 x3) to stay in the flyweight title chase.

mindset.body: Dom does not chase the week — he sequences it. Fierce calm is competitive composure under a real clock: charge first, body second, security skim when ready, admin only when the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may arrive loud; he arrives prepared. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Today is not about proving anything. It is about starting clean so the rest of the week has room to land.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.hed: Begin With the Breath, Not the Storm
grimoire.body: “A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.” (Proverbs 15:1) Solomon’s counsel is not passivity — it is order under pressure. A Monday that opens with charge and clarity outruns one that opens with alarm. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who named what approached before it spoke; you name the morning the same way — breath first, body second, then the board.
grimoire.practice: Before opening any inbox thread, finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener. Refuge first; reaction second.

techDemo.kicker: Fast learn · from your X bookmarks
techDemo.pick: Google’s free Graph & Loop engineering course — 1 prompt → 100 agents → loops → graphs
techDemo.author: @callanxai

image.alt: Prompts to agents to loops to graphs — four-stage diagram

lesson.oneLiner: Stop stuffing one mega-prompt. Promote the work one layer: prompt → agent → loop → graph.
beats: Agent = the worker that runs that job.
Loop = check → retry/route until the job is actually finished (closes work without you).
Graph = the map of many jobs: which exist, in what order, what carries into tomorrow’s run.
lesson.takeaway: One-two dump: a loop finishes a single job; a graph decides which jobs exist and keeps accepted work moving overnight.
